summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists, among others, US, UK, Canadian, German and French passports as visa-free for up to 90 days in 180 days, and says citizens of eligible countries apply for e-Visas online. The UK FCDO says Ukraine's airspace remains closed and its borders with Belarus and Russia are closed; its entry advice covers travel on to Poland, Hungary and Moldova.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace remains closed; its entry advice says to check the travel advice for the country you travel on to.
The UK Foreign Office says to identify shelter locations in advance of any air alert and to take shelter immediately when one is announced; several air raid alert apps exist, including "Air Alert".

The UK FCDO says martial law is in force throughout Ukraine, to expect increased documentation checks and transport restrictions, with curfews among other possible measures, and to carry your passport at all times. Canada's travel advice says to follow the instructions of local authorities at all times, including air raid warning sirens, curfews and evacuation orders.

The UK Foreign Office says Ukrainian national and dual-national males aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving the country, and that the Ukrainian authorities may see you as a Ukrainian national, for example if you have a Ukrainian parent or were born in Ukraine.

The UK FCDO says your travel insurance could be invalidated if you travel against its advice. Canada's travel advice says to make sure you get travel insurance that includes coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ukraine?
faq.answer: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists, among others, US, UK, Canadian, German and French passports as visa-free for up to 90 days in 180 days. It says citizens of eligible countries apply for e-Visas online, and that visa applications are submitted via visa.mfa.gov.ua, where you choose the embassy or visa application centre. The UK FCDO says Ukraine's airspace remains closed.

faq.question: How do I get to Ukraine if there are no flights?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace remains closed and that Ukraine's borders with Belarus and Russia are closed; its entry advice covers travel on to Poland, Hungary and Moldova and says to check the travel advice for those countries.

faq.question: Is it safe to visit Ukraine right now?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Ukraine, with the exception of some western regions, where it advises against all but essential travel. It says to identify shelter locations in advance of any air alert, and that there are air raid alert apps such as "Air Alert". Canada advises avoiding all travel to Ukraine.

faq.question: How does the Ukrainian eVisa work?
faq.answer: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says you register on its e-Visa platform, fill in the application online, upload a photo, passport, health insurance policy with EUR 30,000 coverage, proof of sufficient funds and a document confirming the purpose of the visit, and pay the fee: USD 20 for a single-entry e-Visa, USD 30 for double entry, doubled for the urgent procedure. It says applications are processed within 1 working day (urgent) or 3 working days, and that e-Visas are single or double entry 30-day visas.

faq.question: Do Ukraine's martial-law exit restrictions apply to foreign visitors?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says Ukrainian national and dual-national males aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving the country, and that even if you do not consider Ukrainian your primary nationality, the Ukrainian authorities may see you as a Ukrainian national, for example if you have a Ukrainian parent or were born in Ukraine.

faq.question: Should I bring cash to Ukraine?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says credit cards are widely used in cities, but that ATMs might not be refilled with cash, some bank cards might not be accepted, and ATMs and card terminals may not work during power cuts, and to make sure you have sufficient cash in local currency. Canada's travel advice says you must declare €10,000 or more, or the equivalent, to customs when entering or leaving Ukraine.

levies.text: Ukrainian citizens, foreigners and stateless persons pay the tourist tax when they arrive in an area whose village, town or city council has introduced it and stay in the accommodation listed in the Tax Code. They pay it in advance, before the stay, to the tax agent. The council sets the rate for each day of stay: up to 0.5% of the minimum wage set on 1 January of the tax year for domestic tourism, and up to 5% for inbound tourism, per person per day. Children under 18 do not pay.
